briefings.title: Bill Gurley: Searching for Feynman
briefings.tldr: Bill Gurley examines historical catastrophes (like the 737 MAX, Fukushima, and Challenger) to demonstrate how society successfully investigates failures through independent searchers and root-cause analysis—and contrasts this with the systemic failure to uncover the origins of COVID-19.

briefings.title: Silicon Valley Royalty Bill Gurley On The Dangerous AI Funding Bubble
briefings.tldr: Bill Gurley warns of a starkly polarized venture landscape where AI startups are flooded with capital at dangerous valuations while non-AI firms struggle to raise, emphasizing that excessive funding often masks poor unit economics and creates unsustainable expectations for founders.

briefings.title: What Most People Miss When Using AI | Bill Gurley
briefings.tldr: Long-term success in investing and entrepreneurship requires combining a deep study of historical industry "bedrock" with obsessive learning on the bleeding edge of technological disruptions.

briefings.title: Anthropic's Digital God, Pope vs AI, Job Loss Narrative Flips, Open Source Crackdown Coming?
briefings.tldr: Tech leaders and frontier AI founders are shifting away from the "job apocalypse" narrative toward productivity-driven growth, while a high-stakes battle intensifies over potential government crackdowns on open-source AI and the underlying motivations of creators aiming to build a superior digital species.

briefings.title: Investing in The AI Era, Lessons from China, & Career Advice in 2026 | Bill Gurley

people.name: Jake Humphrey
people.role: Host, The Room Where It Happened

briefings.tldr: Bill Gurley argues that AI is an "infinite game" where the greatest risk is professional inaction; success in this era requires "high agency" curiosity to use AI as a productivity "jet pack" rather than a tool to bypass learning.

briefings.title: Venture capital legend, Bill Gurley.
briefings.tldr: Venture capital legend Bill Gurley argues that long-term career success is driven by "fascination"—a deep, work-driven curiosity—rather than fleeting passion, and warns founders to prioritize peer-group learning and equity retention over reflexive venture capital funding.

briefings.title: Venture capital legend, Bill Gurley.
briefings.tldr: Venture capital legend Bill Gurley argues that long-term career success stems from "fascination"—a deep, work-oriented curiosity—rather than mere passion, and emphasizes that building collaborative peer groups is the most effective way to accelerate professional growth in the AI era.

briefings.title: A Fireside Chat With A Venture Capital Legend
briefings.tldr: To achieve elite career success, professionals must move beyond "passion" toward "fascination"—a deep, obsessive curiosity that fuels the repetitive learning necessary to master nuance and navigate disruptive shifts like AI.

briefings.title: The Misleading Advice Every Entrepreneur Gets Wrong with Bill Gurley
briefings.tldr: Successful careers and high-growth ventures are built on the "30-year test" of long-term sustainability and the exploitation of network effects, often requiring a degree of "healthy self-delusion" to tackle challenges that more experienced leaders might find too daunting.

briefings.title: The AI Divide: Who Wins and Who Gets Replaced | Prof G Markets
briefings.channel: The Prof G Pod – Scott Galloway
briefings.tldr: Legendary venture capitalist Bill Gurley argues that extreme curiosity and high agency are the primary safeguards against AI displacement, while warning that the "institutionalization" of venture capital and "circular" accounting deals are distorting market health and excluding retail investors.

people.name: Anthony Scaramucci
people.role: Founder and Managing Partner, SkyBridge Capital

briefings.tldr: True career security in the age of AI comes from pursuing deep "fascination" rather than traditional safety, as obsessive curiosity fuels the continuous learning and high energy required to reach the top 1% of any field.

briefings.title: How to Live a Life You Won’t Regret at 80 - Bill Gurley
briefings.tldr: The majority of professionals (60–70%) experience "boldness regret"—the psychological weight of inaction—and true career fulfillment requires utilizing the "Regret Minimization Framework" to pivot toward work where continuous learning feels like play rather than a grind.

briefings.title: Full Interview: Bill Gurley Thinks College Kills Creativity
briefings.tldr: True career success stems from "high agency" and hyper-curiosity, traits that allow individuals to utilize AI as a professional superpower rather than a displacement threat in an increasingly competitive and regulated economic landscape.

briefings.title: Bill Gurley
briefings.tldr: Renowned venture capitalist Bill Gurley discusses the mechanics of high-stakes investing, the importance of "fascination" over "passion" in career mastery, and his shift from active investing at Benchmark toward influencing public policy and "disinhibiting" others through his book, Running Down a Dream.
